messages.subject: Wednesday 11/8: intro to brms!
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

We will meet this Wednesday from 12 - 2 pm in the Datalab Classroom (360 Shields library) with a zoom option <https://ucdavis.zoom.us/j/92807937862>.

Wes and I will be leading a mini-workshop introducing the package brms. We will cover some of its capabilities and work through an example of how to specify and evaluate a multilevel model using functions from the package.

We'll then transition to open work time after the workshop for any questions you may have - brms-related and beyond!

See you then,

Your D-RUG Coo[R]dinators
________________________________________________________________
Please remember to post your questions to our Discourse <https://d-rug.discourse.group/> site in advance of attending D-RUG virtually. This helps us do a better job of answering your questions, and also keep a log of the types of questions we see frequently.

For those not familiar with D-RUG, the R Users' Group is a weekly working group to get some help with R-specific coding problems. The coordinators are various and sundry coding connoisseurs, ranging from UCD data scientists to grad students on campus. We meet for 2 hours in an open-forum format, so you can treat D-RUG as a communal, co-working environment: come hang out and chat, work on your own, seek help, make friends. Or, a little bit of everything! Check out our website <https://d-rug.github.io/> for more information.

Mini-workshop schedule:
Nov 15: Debugging tools - Elise
Nov 22: Thanksgiving break
Nov 29: Inla - Wes
Dec 6: aggiedown - Liza/Ryan

messages.subject: Wednesday 11/15: debugging tools
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

We will meet this Wednesday from 12 - 2 pm in the Datalab Classroom (360 Shields library) with a zoom option <https://ucdavis.zoom.us/j/92807937862> for those who are remote.

Elise will lead us through some debugging tools in R to find and fix errors in our code. This session follows up on some of the techniques we discussed earlier in the quarter from the Debugging chapter <https://adv-r.hadley.nz/debugging.html> from Advanced R, but no worries if you did not attend the first session. We will then switch over to open work time for the second half of D-RUG. Come by and work, ask questions, or just say hey!

See you then,
